title: Dasharatha brings Rishyashringa to Ayodhya
introduction: On the advice of his minister Sumantra, Dasharatha proceeds to Anga kingdom to fetch Sage Rishyasringa and his wife Shanta to his capital Ayodhya.
closing: One cycle of the above four eras is called one mahā yugaand seventy-one [71] of such of the Fourfold Eras mahā yugā-swill become one manvantara, Manu-Epoch, the time scale attributed to one Manu, the Supreme Ruler of Mankind. There are total fourteen such Manu-epochs and six of them over in the present manvantara, the time-scale.

The completed Manu cycles are 1.] svayambhu manu, 2.] svārociṣa manu, 3.] auttami manu, 4.] tāmasa manu, 5.] raivata manu, 6.] cākśa manu. Presently we are in the Seventh cycle called vaivasvata mnavantara, and there are seven more manvantara -s to come, starting with 8.] surya sāvarni ṃanu, 9.] dharma sāvarni, 10.] dakśa savarni, 11.] rudra sāvarni, 12.] brahma sāvrani, 13.] roucya manu , 14.] bhoutya manu.

Such fourteen Manu time cycles will be said to be a Day of Brahma, the Absolute. Ramayana is said to have happened in kṛta yuga, the second Manu time cycle. The earlier one is satya yuga, in which the ancestors of Rama, descendants of Raghu dynasty, like Saagara, Harishchandra et al, were the rulers, which is called Ikshvaku dynasty.
इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे एकादशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 11th chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
भूय एव हि राजेन्द्र शृणु मे वचनं हितम् |
यथा स देवप्रवरः कथयामेवमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
bhūya eva hi rājendra śṛṇu me vacanam hitam |
yathā sa devapravaraḥ kathayāmāsa buddhimān
verses.translation: Minister Sumantra continued, "oh, the great king, I will further narrate all that has been said by Sanat Kumara, the best one among all deities, kindly listen to these favourable words." [1-11-1.]
notes: Sage Sanat Kumara belongs to the bygone era of Ikshvaku dynasty. Please refer to the account regarding the era-system if ancient India at endnote.

glosses.meaning: he, that best one among deities [Sage Sanat Kumara]

verses.devanagari:
इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले जातो भविष्यति सुधार्मिकः |
नाम्ना दशरथो राजा श्रीमान्सत्यप्रतिश्रवः
verses.iast:
ikṣvākūṇām kule jāto bhaviṣyati sudhārmikaḥ |
nāmnā daśaratho rājā śrīmān satya pratiśravaḥ
verses.translation: "A king named Dasharatha will be born into Ikshwaku dynasty who will be very virtuous, resplendent and truthful one to his vow." [Said Sanat Kumara, the Sage.]

verses.devanagari:
अङ्गराजेन सख्यं च तस्य राज्ञो भविष्यति |
कन्या चास्य महाभागा शांता नाम भविष्यति
verses.iast:
añga rājena sakhyam ca tasya rājño bhaviṣyati |
kanyā ca asya mahābhāgā śāntā nāma bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: "King Dasharatha will befriend the king of Anga and the king of Anga will beget a fortunate girl named Shanta.
notes: Shanta is said to be the daughter of Dasharatha and given to Romapada in adoption, and Rishyasringa marries her alone. This is j~n Sumantra says to Dasharatha at 1-9-19.

verses.devanagari:
पुत्रस्तु सोऽङ्गराजस्य रोमपाद इति श्रुतः |
तं स राजा दशरथो गमिष्यति महायशाः
verses.iast:
putrastuḥ añgasya rājñaḥ tu romapāda iti śrutaḥ |
tam sa rājā daśaratho gamiṣyati mahāyaśāḥ
verses.translation: The son of the king of Anga, the earlier king of Anga kingdom, will be known as Romapada, or also know as Chitraratha, and the highly renowned king Dasharatha approaches Romapada.

glosses.itrans: saH putraH tu angasya raajnaH tu
glosses.iast: saḥ putraḥ tu angasya rājnaḥ tu
glosses.devanagari: सः पुत्रः तु अन्गस्य राज्नः तु

verses.devanagari:
अनपत्योऽस्मि धर्मात्मन् शांताभर्ता मम क्रतुम् |
आहरेत त्वयाज्ञप्तः संतानार्थं कुलस्य च
verses.iast:
anapatyo'smi dharmātman śāntā bhartā mama kratum |
āhareta tvayā ājñaptaḥ santānārtham kulasya ca
verses.translation: Then king Dasharatha says to king of Anga "oh, righteous one, I am childless and hence I intend to perform a Vedic ritual. Let the husband of your daughter Shanta, Sage Rishyasringa, preside over that Vedic ritual at you behest, for the sake of progeny in my dynasty.

glosses.meaning: for my, dynasty, for progeny, for the sake of

verses.devanagari:
श्रुत्वा राज्ञोऽथ तद्वाक्यं मनसा स विचिंत्य च |
प्रदास्यते पुत्रवन्तं शांताभर्तारमात्मवान्
verses.iast:
śrutvā rājño'tha tat vākyam manasā sa vicintya ca |
pradāsyate putravantam śāntā bhartāram ātmavān
verses.translation: "On hearing those words of king Dasharatha that benevolent soul Romapada, the king of Anga, considers heartily and agrees to send the one who endows progeny by rituals, namely Sage Rishyasringa his son-in-law.
notes: The words pradāsyate putravantam are read in some translations as 'Rishyasringa who already has a son...' while others read it as 'a sage who endows progeny by putra kameṣṭi ritual...' But in Maha Bharata father Vibhandaka says to Rishyasringa to comeback after begetting a son, which Rishyasringa did not concede. So taking this some say Rishyasringa has a son. But it is generally accepted that putravantam as āhitāgni, Vedic ritualist of eminence, according to: jāta putraḥ kṛśṇa keśo agnīn adhīta...according to śruti scripture.

glosses.meaning: one who has son / or, one who endows sons

verses.devanagari:
प्रतिगृह्य च तं विप्रं स राजा विगतज्वरः |
आहरिष्यति तं यज्ञं प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना
verses.iast:
pratigṛhyam ca tam vipram sa rājā vigata jvaraḥ |
āhariṣyati tam yajñam prahṛṣṭena antarātmanā
verses.translation: "On receiving that Brahman, Sage Rishyasringa, at the behest of his father-in-law, that king Dasharatha gets rid of his febrile condition and will accomplish that Vedic ritual, feeling very felicitous in the depths of his heart.

glosses.meaning: very felicitousness, in depths of heart

verses.devanagari:
तं च राजा दशरथो यष्टुकामः कृतांजलिः |
ऋष्यशृङ्गं द्विजश्रेष्ठं वरयिष्यति धर्मवित्
यज्ञार्थं प्रसवार्थं च स्वर्गार्थं च नरेश्वरः |
लभते च स तं कामं द्विजमुख्याद्विशांपतिः
verses.iast:
tam ca rājā daśaratho yaśas kāmaḥ kṛtāṃliḥ |
ṛṣyaśṛñgam dvija śreṣṭham varayiṣyati dharmavit
yajñārtham prasavārtham ca svargārtham ca nareśvaraḥ |
labhate ca sa tam kāmam dvija mukhyāt viśāmpatiḥ
verses.translation: "That king, the desirer of glory, the knower of virtue and the lord of people, namely Dasharatha will be requesting that best Brahman Rishyasringa with his palms adjoined in supplication for the conduct of ritual, for progeny and even for his heavenly abodes, and that king of all the quarters of earth will accomplish those desires from that eminent Brahman Rishyasringa.
notes: Heavenly abodes are dependent on begetting sons:aputrasya gatir nāsti svargo naivaca naivaca There is no way out [in other worlds] for those without sons... śruti scripture. Hence the request of Dasharatha is that way.

glosses.meaning: he that, to [all the] quarters of earth, king of - king [Dasharatha]

verses.devanagari:
पुत्राश्चास्य भविष्यन्ति चत्वारोऽमितविक्रमाः |
वंशप्रतिष्ठानकराः सर्वभूतेषु विश्रुताः
verses.iast:
putrāḥ ca asya bhaviṣyanti catvāro amita vikramāḥ |
vaṃśa pratiṣṭhānakarāḥ sarva būteṣu viśrutāḥ
verses.translation: "There will be four sons to king Dasharatha that abound with valour, enrich dynasty's reputation and they will be renowned among all beings." Thus said Sage Sanat Kumara to other sages.
notes: 'Sons and Paradise are intimately connected in Indian belief. A man desires above every thing to have a son to perpetuate his race, and to assist with sacrifices and funeral rites to make him worthy to obtain a lofty seat in heaven or to preserve that which he has already obtained.' Gorresio via Ralph T. H. Griffith [1870-1874].

glosses.meaning: sons, also, to him [Dasharatha,] will be

verses.devanagari:
एवं स देवप्रवरः पूर्वं कथितवान्कथाम् |
सनत्कुमारो भगवान्पुरा देवयुगे प्रभुः
verses.iast:
evam sa deva pravaraḥ pūrvam kathitavān kathām |
sanatkumāro bhagavān purā devayuge prabhuḥ
verses.translation: "This way he that ancient and godly Sage Sanatkumaara, who is also Brahma's brain-child like Narada, said this legend in earlier Divine Era, called krita yuga..." thus Sumantra continued his narration to Dasharatha.
notes: Comment: Please refer endnote for yuga / era classification.

glosses.meaning: earlier, in previous, Divine Era, [krita yuga,] narration, he narrated.

verses.devanagari:
स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल तमानय सुसत्कृतम् |
स्वयमेव महाराज गत्वा सबलवाहनः
verses.iast:
sa tvam puruṣa śārdūla samānaya susatkṛtam |
svayam eva mahārāja gatvā sa bala vāhanaḥ
verses.translation: " Oh, great king the manly-tiger, he that Sage Rishyasringa be led here on your proceeding in person with staff and transport and on adoring him well personally." Thus Sumantra concluded his narration.

glosses.itrans: saha bala vaahanaH svayam eva gatvaa
glosses.iast: saha bala vāhanaḥ svayam eva gatvā
glosses.devanagari: सह बल वाहनः स्वयं एव गत्वा
glosses.meaning: with, staff, transport in person, only, on proceeding

verses.devanagari:
सुमंत्रस्य वचः श्रुत्वा हृष्टो दशरथोऽभवत् |
अनुमान्य वसिष्ठं च सूतवाक्यं निशम्य च
सान्तःपुरः सहामात्यः प्रययौ यत्र स द्विजः |
verses.iast:
sumantrasya vacaḥ śrutvā hṛṣṭo daśaratho'bhavat |
anumānya vasiṣṭham ca sūtavākyam niśāṃya ca
sa antaḥpuraḥ saha amātyaḥ prayayau yatra sa dvijaḥ |
verses.translation: On hearing the word of advise from charioteer, Dasharatha became gladsome and made Sumantra to reiterate to that sage also, for his approval, then Dasharatha travelled to the place where that Brahman Rishyasringa is, along with the inmates of palace-chambers and ministers too.
notes: While the chief priest Vashishta is officiator of all rituals no king can invite another priest to perform something without the consent of the officiating priest. Hence the consent of Vasishta is obtained, after asking Sumantra to reiterate j~n all was said, to sage Vashishta also. anena prācīna ṛtvik abhyanujñanena na eva anya āneyaḥ -- dharmākūtam

glosses.meaning: on getting those words listened b Vashishta from Sumantra - on reporting, also
making [Vashishta ] agreeable [to the words of Sumantra,] even
travelled to, where, that, Brahman is there.

verses.devanagari:
वनानि सरितश्चैव व्यतिक्रम्य शनैः शनैः
अभिचक्राम तं देशं यत्र वै मुनिपुंगवः |
verses.iast:
vanāni saritaḥ ca eva vyatikraṃya śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
abhicakrāma tam deśam yatra vai munipuṅgavaḥ |
verses.translation: On crossing over the rivers and forests slowly and steadily Dasharatha entered that kingdom where that eminent Brahman is there.

verses.devanagari:
आसाद्य तं द्विजश्रेष्ठं रोमपादसमीपगम्
ऋषिपुत्रं ददर्शाथो दीप्यमानमिवानलम् |
verses.iast:
āsādya tam dvija śreṣṭham romapāda samīpagam
ṛṣiputram dadarśa atho dīpyamānam iva analam |
verses.translation: Then Dasharatha saw that best Brahman who he is nearby king Romapada, andwho is resplendent like ritual fire.

glosses.meaning: with Romapada, one who is nearby

verses.devanagari:
ततो राजा यथायोग्यं पूजां चक्रे विशेषतः
सखित्वात्तस्य वै राज्ञः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना |
verses.iast:
tato rājā yathā yogyam pūjām cakre viśeṣataḥ
sakhitvāt tasya vai rājñaḥ prahṛṣṭena antarātmanā |
verses.translation: Then king Romapada gladdened at heart of hearts paid excellent respects to king Dasharatha procedurally and in view of their friendship.

verses.devanagari:
रोमपादेन चाख्यातमृषिपुत्राय धीमते
सख्यं संबन्धकं चैव तदा तं प्रत्यपूजयत् |
verses.iast:
romapādena ca ākhyātam ṛṣiputrāya dhīmate
sakhyam sambandhakam caiva tadā tam pratyapūjayat |
verses.translation: Then Romapada informed the wise sage Rishyasringa about the friendship and relation with Dasharatha, and then that sage worshipped king Dasharatha in his return.

glosses.meaning: to the wise one, sage's son � Rishyasringa, is informed
then, him, [Rishyasringa] in return, adored [ Dasharatha.]

verses.devanagari:
एवं सुसत्कृतस्तेन सहोषित्वा नरर्षभः
सप्ताष्टदिवसान् राजा राजानमिदमब्रवीत् |
verses.iast:
evam susatkṛtaḥ tena sahoṣitvā nararṣabhaḥ
saptāṣṭa divasān rājā rājānam idam abravīt |
verses.translation: Thus well received by king Romapada, king Dasharatha spent seven to eight days with him, and then spoke this to king Romapada.

glosses.meaning: man, the sacred bull, king - Dasharatha

verses.devanagari:
शांता तव सुता राजन् सह भर्त्रा विशांपते
मदीयं नगरं यातु कार्यं हि महदुद्यतम् |
verses.iast:
śāntā tava sutā rājan saha bhartrā viśām pate
madīyam nagaram yātu kāryam hi mahadudyatam |
verses.translation: "Oh, lord of subjects, your daughter Princess Shanta may go over my city Ayodhya along with her husband Rishyasringa, as oh, king, I am contemplating to perform a great Vedic ritual, indeed." So said Dasharatha to Romapada.

glosses.meaning: my, city, she may go over
a great, deed - the ritual, is contemplated by me, indeed.

verses.devanagari:
तथेति राजा संश्रुत्य गमनं तस्य धीमतः
उवाच वचनं विप्रं गच्छ त्वं सह भार्यया |
verses.iast:
tathā iti rājā saṃśrutya gamanam tasya dhīmataḥ
uvāca vacanam vipram gaccha tvam saha bhāryayā |
verses.translation: "So it shall be" said king Romapada agreeing to their travel with king Dasharatha, and addressed these words to that Brahman sage and his son-in-law, Sage Rishyasringa "You may proceed along with your wife."
notes: Here Ralph T. H. Griffith's translation [1870-1874] has that Shanta is the daughter of Dasharatha: 'This king,' he said, 'from days of old / A well beloved friend I hold. / To me this pearl of dames he gave / From childless woe mine age to save, / The daughter whom he loved so much, / Moved by compassion's gentle touch. / In him thy S'anta's father see: / As I am even so is he...

glosses.meaning: of that intellectual one, his - Rishyasringa's travel
= you, your wife, along with, shall proceed

verses.devanagari:
ऋषिपुत्रः प्रतिश्रुत्य तथेत्याह नृपं तदा
स नृपेणाभ्यनुज्ञातः प्रययौ सह भार्यया |
verses.iast:
ṛṣiputraḥ pratiśrutya tathā iti āhaḥ nṛpam tadā
sa nṛpeṇa abhyanujñātaḥ prayayau saha bhāryayā |
verses.translation: Then Rishyasringa agreed and replied to the king Romapada "So it will be done" and then having been permitted by the king he set forth along with his wife.

verses.devanagari:
तावन्योन्यांजलिं कृत्वा स्नेहात्संश्लिष्य चोरसा
ननंदतुर्दशरथो रोमपादश्च वीर्यवान् |
verses.iast:
tāva anyonya añjalim kṛtvā snehāt saṃśliṣya ca urasā
nanandatuḥ daśaratho romapādaḥ ca vīryavān |
verses.translation: Those valiant kings greeted each other with thanksgiving palm-fold, and in friendship they embraced each other and gladdened.

glosses.meaning: those two - Dasharatha and Romapada, valiant kings
to each other, thanksgiving with palm-fold

verses.devanagari:
ततः सुहृदमापृच्छ्य प्रस्थितो रघुनन्दनः
पौरेभ्यः प्रेषयामास दूतान्वै शीघ्रगामिनः |
verses.iast:
tataḥ suhṛdam āpṛcchya prasthito raghunandanaḥ
paureṣu preṣayāmāsa dūtān vai śīghra gāminaḥ |
verses.translation: Then king Dasharatha who set forth to Ayodhya bade farewell to his friend king Romapada, and he firstly sent quick-footed messengers to Ayodhya to inform his citizens about his arrival along with Sage Rishyasringa.

verses.devanagari:
क्रियतां नगरं सर्वं क्षिप्रमेव स्वलंकृतम्
धूपितं सिक्तसम्मृष्टं पताकाभिरलंकृतम् |
verses.iast:
kriyatām nagaram sarvam kṣipram eva svalaṅkṛtam
dhūpitam sikta sammṛṣṭam patākābhiḥ alaṅkṛtam |
verses.translation: "Let the entire city of Ayodhya be well decorated very quickly, let her streets be sprinkled with water and then swept, let the flags of welcome be hoisted.." Thus, king Dasharatha ordered messengers that are sent beforehand.

glosses.meaning: [streets be] water sprinkled well, and then swept

verses.devanagari:
ततः प्रहृष्टाः पौरास्ते श्रुत्वा राजानमागतम्
तथा प्रचक्रुस्तत्सर्वं राज्ञा यत्प्रेषितं तदा |
verses.iast:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭāḥ paurāḥ te śrutvā rājānam āgatam
tathā cakruḥ ca tat sarvam rājñā yat preṣitam tadā |
verses.translation: Then on hearing the arrival of their king all the citizens felt very happy and readily performed all those works exactly as ordered by their king.

verses.devanagari:
ततः स्वलंकृतं राजा नगरं प्रविवेश ह
शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैः पुरस्कृत्य द्विजर्षभम् |
verses.iast:
tataḥ svalaṅkṛtam rājā nagaram praviveśa ha
śañkha dundubhi nihrā.rdaiḥ puraskṛtvā dvijarṣabham |
verses.translation: Then king Dasharatha keeping Rishyasringa before him entered the well-decorated city Ayodhya amidst the full sounding of conch shells and drumbeats.

verses.devanagari:
ततः प्रमुदिताः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा तं नागरा द्विजम्
प्रवेश्यमानं सत्कृत्य नरेन्द्रेणेन्द्रकर्मणा |
यथा दिवि सुरेन्द्रेण सहस्राक्षेण काश्यपम्
verses.iast:
tataḥ pramuditāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā tam nāgarā dvijam
praveśyamānam satkṛtya narendreṇa indra karmaṇā |
yathā divi surendreṇa sahasrākśeṇa kāśyapam
verses.translation: Then all the citizens are very happy on seeing that Brahman, Sage Rishyasringa, who is well honoured and being entered into the city by their king Dasharatha, as has been done once by Indra when he entered sage Kashyapa's son Vamana, the dwarfish boy and the incarnation of Vishnu, into heavens, and thus those citizens felt that their human lord Dasharatha vies with divine lord Indra.
notes: The simile of Indra to king Dasharatha is in two ways. Dasharatha ruled kingdom like Indra who rules Heavens. The word Indra karmaṇa also refers to the deeds of Dasharatha, in helping the gods' forces combating the demonic forces. Thus the deeds performed by Dasharatha are like those of Indra's. Here Dasharatha is bringing Sage Rishyasringa to Ayodhya. Earlier Indra led Vamana, the dwarf-boy to heavens. Vamana is the incarnation of Vishnu in early ages and after Vamana suppressed Bali, the Emperor to netherworlds, Indra took Vamana to heavens. Thus Dasharatha is like Indra on earth, both by his virtue and deed. Incidentally, Vamana i.e., Vishnu, is the son-incarnate to Sage Kaashyapa, while sage Rishyasringa is the grandson of the same Kaashyapa. Thus Sage Kaashyapa is instrumental to these two incarnations. Through the divine grace of Sage Rishyasringa, the same Vishnu is going to take birth as Rama, while Sage Kashyapa is a grandparent of Rama in this era, and while he alone was Vishnu's father when Vishnu incarnated as Dwarf boy Vamana.

glosses.meaning: one who has exploits like that of Indra
sage Kashyapa's son, namely Vamana, the dwarf boy incarnation of Vishnu
by thousand eyed, lord of gods, namely Indra

verses.devanagari:
अन्तःपुरं प्रवेश्यैनं पूजां कृत्वा च शास्त्रतः |
कृतकृत्यं तदात्मानं मेने तस्योपवाहनात्
verses.iast:
antaḥpuram praveśya enam pūjām kṛtvā ca śāstrataḥ |
kṛtakṛtyam tadā ātmānam mene tasya upavāhanāt
verses.translation: Dasharatha entered the sage into the palace chambers and worshipped him there as ordained in the scriptures, and in bringing the Sage here into his country, king Dasharatha believed that his desired is fulfilled.

verses.devanagari:
अन्तःपुरस्त्रियः सर्वाः शांतां दृष्ट्वा तथागताम् |
सह भर्त्रा विशालाक्षीं प्रीत्यानंदमुपागमन्
verses.iast:
antaḥpurāṇi sarvāṇi śāntām dṛṣṭvā tathā āgatām |
saha bhartrā viśālākṣīm prītyā ānandam upāgaman
verses.translation: On seeing her, the broad-eyed Shanta, who came there along with her husband all the ladies of palace derived happiness for the homecoming of their own daughter, as it were.

glosses.meaning: her husband, along with, one who arrived

verses.devanagari:
पूज्यमाना तु ताभिः सा राज्ञा चैव विशेषतः |
उवास तत्र सुखिता कञ्चित्कालं सहर्त्विजा
verses.iast:
pūjyamānā tu tābhiḥ sā rājñā ca eva viśeṣataḥ |
uvāsa tatra sukhitā kancit kālam saha dvijā
verses.translation: Shanta thus being admired by all of them, and in an exceptional manner by Dasharatha, comfortably resided there along with her husband, the Vedic scholar Rishyasringa.
notes: The Riwik is not just a reciter of Veda-s but more a director or conductor of whole orchestration of the Vedic ritual, which involves lots of rules, in reciting hymns, in performing deeds and all in their exactness. The whole lots of works that need be performed have the order of precedence like prime, auxiliary or adjunctive in their ordinance. A Ritwik is the elated scholar who keeps track of these activities while other scholars recite hymns as directed by these Ritwik-s. Hence, Ritwik-hood is the highest.

glosses.meaning: that, Vedic scholar - her husband, along with
